title: A first-time voter's polling day
body: Meera turned 18 this year and registered as a voter through the ECI's online portal. On polling day for the state assembly election, she went to the polling station with her father and her elder brother, who uses a wheelchair. The station had a ramp, a wheelchair and volunteers who guided them to the booth, and police personnel were on guard outside. Inside, a polling officer checked Meera's name on the electoral roll and marked her finger with indelible ink. After she pressed the button against her chosen candidate on the EVM, a printed slip showing the candidate's name and symbol appeared behind a glass window for a few seconds before dropping into a sealed box. That evening Meera learnt that her 88-year-old grandmother had already voted at home, where polling officials had visited with a ballot. Her father also told her that, a week earlier, he had received a forwarded message falsely claiming that the polling date had been changed.
